fields.label: Function
fields.note: Atlassian board fieldset 'WHAT FUNCTION MATCHES YOU?'. The board is rendered in full, so ?team= is URL state the client applies to the loaded rows.

fields.label: Eligible location
fields.note: Atlassian board fieldset 'WHERE ARE YOU ELIGIBLE TO WORK?' (country level); ?location= is URL state applied client-side.

notes: loom.com/careers answers HTTP 308 with Location https://www.atlassian.com/company/careers/all-jobs?team=&location=&search=Loom (Loom is an Atlassian product), so the parent Atlassian board is the only listing. That page renders all 339 rows and its search input is empty, i.e. ?search=Loom is not applied server-side; ?team=Engineering&location=&search= returned the same 339 rows and the same advertised count. The keyword box, the Function fieldset and the Location fieldset filter the already-loaded rows in the browser, so the scraper applies every filter locally over the collected set.
evidence: https://www.atlassian.com/company/careers/all-jobs?team=&location=&search=Loom (339 rows; 17 function options, 15 location options; search input value '')
